violated_contract: A sign-in flow that obtains a user identity and then derives a narrower credential from it (a developer API key minted from a Firebase session) must persist whichever of the two each shipped command needs, not only the derivative. When the flow stores the derivative alone and a later command gates on the identity, that command is unreachable through every supported login, and its own error message sends the user back to the flow that produced the rejected profile. Nothing in the unit suite notices: the command's tests hand-craft the profile shape the login never writes.
canonical_prevention: Keep the identity on the profile beside the derived credential and let each command pick the credential its route accepts through one explicit seam (a session flag on the client builder) rather than through the profile's auth-method label. A regression test must run the real login command end to end against mocked providers and then run the identity-gated command on the profile that login actually wrote, asserting the bearer token each route received; tests that start from a hand-written profile do not count as coverage of the login path.
